paragraphs: Storm Austen brought very heavy rain to Ireland on Thursday night and Friday morning.

Met Éireann had an orange rain warning for Cork, Kerry and Waterford until 5am on Friday. There was also an orange warning for Dublin, Wexford and Wicklow from 2am to 8am on Friday. A yellow warning for all of Leinster and Munster ended at 10am.
Rivers like the Liffey, the Lee and the Slaney may get very full. There may be floods in the south and east until Saturday. Trains and buses may be late.
Another storm, called Boelo, may come on Saturday. It will be very windy at sea. There may be floods on the west coast.
Stay away from the sea and rivers. Do not walk or drive in flood water. Never touch electric wires on the ground. Check met.ie before you travel.
Storm Austen brought heavy rain and strong winds to much of Ireland on Thursday night and Friday morning, and the risk of flooding will continue into the weekend.

Met Éireann put an orange rain warning on Cork, Kerry and Waterford from 10pm on Thursday until 5am on Friday. Another orange warning covered Dublin, Wexford and Wicklow from 2am to 8am on Friday. A yellow rain and wind warning for all of Leinster and Munster lasted until 10am on Friday.

The rain is moving away, but rivers such as the Liffey, Barrow, Lee, Suir, Nore and Slaney may become very full. There may be flooding in the south, south-east and east until Saturday, and trains and buses may be delayed.

A second storm, called Boelo, is expected on Saturday, at the same time as high tides. This means big waves could flood parts of the west and north-west coasts. Very strong winds are forecast at sea all day on Saturday.

Officials say people should tie down bins and garden furniture, stay away from the coast and rivers, and never touch fallen power lines. Keep a torch and a charged phone ready, and check met.ie before travelling.
Storm Austen swept across Ireland overnight on Thursday, bringing intense rain and strong winds, and the threat of flooding is set to continue into the weekend as a second storm approaches.

Met Éireann issued a Status Orange rain warning for Cork, Kerry and Waterford, valid from 10pm on Thursday until 5am on Friday, and another for Dublin, Wexford and Wicklow from 2am to 8am on Friday. A Status Yellow rain and wind warning covered Leinster and Munster until 10am on Friday, while storm-force winds were forecast off the south coast.
